sections.name: Physics
sections.description: Units, laws of motion, optics, electricity, waves, and inventions

questions.question: The SI unit of electric current is ____.
questions.explanation: Named after André-Marie Ampère, 1 ampere equals 1 coulomb of charge passing per second.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Newton is the force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s².

questions.question: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is called a ____.
questions.explanation: Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.

questions.question: Light travels fastest in ____.
questions.explanation: In a vacuum, light travels at approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.question: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another is called ____.
questions.explanation: Refraction occurs because the speed of light changes when entering a medium of different optical density.

questions.question: The SI unit of electrical resistance is ____.
questions.explanation: According to Ohm's Law, R = V / I, measured in Ohms (Ω).

questions.question: The blue colour of the sky is primarily due to ____ of light.
questions.explanation: Shorter blue wavelengths scatter more strongly by atmospheric molecules (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.question: Sound waves cannot travel through a ____.
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and requires a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate.

questions.question: The device used to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy is a ____.
questions.explanation: A generator works on Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: The SI unit of frequency is ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Hertz equals one cycle per second.

questions.question: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using a ____ lens.
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges incoming light rays so they focus directly on the retina.

questions.question: The SI unit of power is ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Watt is equal to 1 Joule of work done per second.

questions.question: A fuse wire is made of an alloy of tin and ____.
questions.explanation: A tin-lead alloy has high resistance and a low melting point, protecting circuits from overload.

sections.name: Biology
sections.description: Cell biology, human anatomy, vitamins, diseases, and botany

questions.question: The powerhouse of the cell is the ____.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes ____.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is essential for collagen synthesis; its lack causes bleeding gums and scurvy.

questions.question: The universal donor blood group is ____.
questions.explanation: O-negative red blood cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens.

questions.question: The green pigment in plants responsible for photosynthesis is ____.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy (mostly red and blue wavelengths) to convert CO₂ and water into glucose.

questions.question: The longest bone in the human body is the ____.
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is both the longest and strongest bone in the human body.

questions.question: Insulin is secreted by the ____ gland.
questions.explanation: Beta cells in the Islets of Langerhans of the pancreas produce insulin to regulate blood glucose.

questions.question: The largest organ of the human body is the ____.
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest external organ; the liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes ____ in children.
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps absorb calcium; its deficiency leads to soft, weak bones (rickets).

questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney is the ____.
questions.explanation: Each human kidney contains roughly one million nephrons that filter blood to form urine.

questions.question: Plants transport water from roots to leaves through ____ tissue.
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and minerals upward; phloem transports food.

questions.question: The normal resting pH of human blood is approximately ____.
questions.explanation: Human blood is slightly alkaline, maintained tightly between 7.35 and 7.45.

questions.question: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin ____.
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is required to form rhodopsin, a pigment needed for low-light vision.

questions.question: The smallest bone in the human body is the ____.
questions.explanation: The stapes is one of the three ossicles located in the middle ear.

sections.name: Chemistry
sections.description: Periodic table, acids & bases, alloys, formulas, and everyday chemistry

questions.question: The chemical symbol for Gold is ____.
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, 'aurum'.

questions.question: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is ____.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere, followed by Oxygen (~21%).

questions.question: The pH value of pure neutral water at 25°C is ____.
questions.explanation: A pH of 7 is neutral; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic/alkaline.

questions.question: Dry ice is the solid form of ____.
questions.explanation: Solid CO₂ sublimates directly from solid to gas at -78.5°C.

questions.question: The hardest naturally occurring substance is ____.
questions.explanation: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon with a tetrahedral covalent lattice.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy of copper and ____.
questions.explanation: Brass = Copper + Zinc; Bronze = Copper + Tin.

questions.question: The acid present in vinegar is ____ acid.
questions.explanation: Vinegar typically contains 5–8% acetic acid (CH₃COOH).

questions.question: The only metal that is liquid at room temperature is ____.
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) melts at -38.83°C; Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Washing soda is chemically known as sodium ____.
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O); baking soda is sodium bicarbonate.

questions.question: Laughing gas is chemically known as ____ oxide.
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) is used as a mild anesthetic and propellant.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element equals the number of ____ in its nucleus.
questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) is defined by the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.question: Rusting of iron is an example of ____.
questions.explanation: Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (rust).

sections.name: Indian Polity
sections.description: Constitution, Parliament, Fundamental Rights, Schedules, and governance

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November ____.
questions.explanation: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was Dr. ____.
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee appointed on 29 August 1947.

questions.question: The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is ____ years.
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha minimum age is 25 years; Rajya Sabha is 30 years; President/Governor is 35 years.

questions.question: The ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the ____ of India.
questions.explanation: Under Article 64, the Vice President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of the ____ Committee.
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations led to the 42nd Amendment (1976), adding Part IVA.

questions.question: The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) was borrowed from the Constitution of ____.
questions.explanation: Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution draws inspiration from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: The ____ Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of 22 recognized languages.
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages and now recognizes 22 languages.

questions.question: The Anti-Defection Law is contained in the ____ Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: Added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, the Tenth Schedule deals with disqualification on grounds of defection.

questions.question: The guardian and final interpreter of the Indian Constitution is the ____.
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India upholds constitutional supremacy through judicial review.

questions.question: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the ____.
questions.explanation: Under Article 109, a Money Bill can only originate in the Lok Sabha with the President's prior recommendation.

questions.question: The maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed ____ months.
questions.explanation: Article 85 mandates that no more than six months shall intervene between two parliamentary sessions.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed by the ____.
questions.explanation: Under Article 148, the President appoints the CAG for a term of 6 years or up to age 65.

sections.name: Articles & Amendments
sections.description: Important Constitutional Articles and landmark Amendments

questions.question: Article ____ of the Indian Constitution abolishes Untouchability.
questions.explanation: Article 17 makes the practice of untouchability a punishable offence.

questions.question: Article ____ guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.
questions.explanation: Article 21 states: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.'

questions.question: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article ____ the 'Heart and Soul' of the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering the Supreme Court to issue writs.

questions.question: The ____ Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'.
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble and introduced Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: The ____ Amendment Act lowered the voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years.
questions.explanation: Enacted in 1988 (effective 1989), the 61st Amendment amended Article 326.

questions.question: Panchayati Raj institutions were given constitutional status by the ____ Amendment Act, 1992.
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced by the ____ Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment introduced GST across India from 1 July 2017.

questions.question: Article ____ deals with the Uniform Civil Code for citizens.
questions.explanation: Article 44 (under DPSP) directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code throughout India.

questions.question: Article ____ empowers Parliament to amend the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Part XX, Article 368 outlines the procedure for amending the Constitution.

questions.question: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was inserted by the ____ Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment made free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14.

questions.question: Article ____ deals with the Election Commission of India.
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.

questions.question: Article ____ provides for the Finance Commission of India.
questions.explanation: The President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years under Article 280.

questions.question: The ____ Amendment Act (1978) removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment shifted Right to Property from Article 31 to Article 300A.

sections.name: National Parks
sections.description: National Parks, Biosphere Reserves, and Wildlife Sanctuaries of India

questions.question: India's first National Park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, is ____ National Park.
questions.explanation: Located in Uttarakhand, Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the ____.
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is a UNESCO World Heritage Site housing two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses.

questions.question: Gir National Park, the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion, is located in ____.
questions.explanation: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Junagadh/Gir Somnath, Gujarat.

questions.question: The world's only floating National Park, Keibul Lamjao, is situated in ____.
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park floats on Loktak Lake in Manipur and is home to the Sangai deer.

questions.question: Sundarbans National Park, famous for Royal Bengal Tigers and mangroves, is in ____.
questions.explanation: Sundarbans lies in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta in West Bengal.

questions.question: The largest National Park in India by area is ____ National Park in Ladakh.
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park (Ladakh) covers ~4,400 sq km and is famous for snow leopards.

questions.question: Dachigam National Park, famous for the Hangul (Kashmir Stag), is located in ____.
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park is located near Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.question: Silent Valley National Park is located in the Nilgiri Hills of ____.
questions.explanation: Silent Valley in Palakkad, Kerala is famous for its tropical evergreen forests and lion-tailed macaque.

questions.question: Ranthambore National Park is located in the state of ____.
questions.explanation: Located in Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan, Ranthambore is a major Project Tiger reserve.

questions.question: Bandipur National Park is situated in the state of ____.
questions.explanation: Bandipur is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in Chamarajanagar district, Karnataka.

questions.question: Simlipal National Park is located in ____.
questions.explanation: Simlipal is a tiger reserve and biosphere reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha.

questions.question: Kanha National Park, which inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book', is in ____.
questions.explanation: Kanha Tiger Reserve is located in Madhya Pradesh and is known for the Barasingha (swamp deer).

sections.name: All PM Yojanas
sections.description: Pradhan Mantri Yojanas & flagship Government of India schemes

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on 28 August 2014, is India's flagship ____ inclusion mission.
questions.explanation: PMJDY aims to ensure universal access to banking facilities, zero-balance accounts, RuPay cards, and insurance.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) provides free ____ connections to women from BPL households.
questions.explanation: Launched on 1 May 2016 in Ballia, UP, PMUY promotes clean cooking fuel.

questions.question: Under Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY), eligible families receive health cover up to ₹____ lakh per family per year.
questions.explanation: Launched in September 2018, PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh annual secondary and tertiary hospitalization cover.

questions.question: Under PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi), eligible farmer families receive ₹____ per year in three equal installments.
questions.explanation: Farmers receive ₹2,000 every four months (total ₹6,000/year) via Direct Benefit Transfer.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana provides collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh under three categories: Shishu, Kishore, and ____.
questions.explanation: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).

questions.question: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Yojana was launched on 22 January 2015 from Panipat, ____.
questions.explanation: The scheme aims to address the declining Child Sex Ratio and promote girls' education.

questions.question: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October ____.
questions.explanation: Launched on Gandhi Jayanti 2014 to achieve universal sanitation coverage and an Open Defecation Free India.

questions.question: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is open to Indian citizens aged between 18 and ____ years.
questions.explanation: Subscribers aged 18–40 receive guaranteed minimum monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after age 60.

questions.question: PM SVANidhi scheme provides micro-credit working capital loans to ____.
questions.explanation: Launched in June 2020, PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi supports urban street vendors.

questions.question: PM Vishwakarma Yojana, launched in September 2023, supports traditional ____ and craftspeople.
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma provides skill training, toolkit incentives, and collateral-free credit to 18 traditional trades.

questions.question: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to provide up to ____ units of free electricity per month via rooftop solar.
questions.explanation: Launched in February 2024, it subsidizes rooftop solar installations for 1 crore households.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) offers a life insurance cover of ₹____ lakh.
questions.explanation: PMJJBY provides ₹2 lakh life cover for individuals aged 18–50 years.

sections.name: Geography, Rivers & Dams
sections.description: Rivers, dams, mountain passes, lakes, and Indian/World geography

questions.question: The longest river in India is the ____.
questions.explanation: The Ganga flows for about 2,525 km through India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: The highest dam in India is the ____ Dam in Uttarakhand.
questions.explanation: Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi River stands at 260.5 meters.

questions.question: The longest dam in India is the ____ Dam built across the Mahanadi River.
questions.explanation: Located in Odisha, Hirakud Dam stretches about 25.8 km including dykes.

questions.question: The largest freshwater lake in India is ____ Lake in Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Bandipora district is fed by the Jhelum River.

questions.question: The river known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' is the ____.
questions.explanation: The Kosi River frequently shifts its course and causes severe floods in Bihar.

questions.question: The ____ Strait separates India from Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait connects the Bay of Bengal with the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through ____ Indian states.
questions.explanation: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.question: The largest brackish water lagoon in India is ____ Lake in Odisha.
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is the largest coastal lagoon in India and a Ramsar wetland.

questions.question: The longest river in Peninsular India (also called Dakshin Ganga) is the ____.
questions.explanation: Originating at Trimbakeshwar (Maharashtra), the Godavari is ~1,465 km long.

questions.question: Nathu La pass connects Sikkim with ____.
questions.explanation: Nathu La is a mountain pass in the Himalayas at ~4,310 meters.

sections.name: Awards, Dances & Orgs
sections.description: Classical dances, awards, international organizations, and sports

questions.question: The classical dance form Kuchipudi originated in the state of ____.
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi takes its name from Kuchelapuram village in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Kathakali is a classical dance form of ____.
questions.explanation: Both Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dance forms of Kerala.

questions.question: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in ____.
questions.explanation: WHO, WTO, ILO, and WIPO are all headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: The headquarters of UNESCO is located in ____.
questions.explanation: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) is based in Paris.

questions.question: India's highest civilian award is the ____.
questions.explanation: Instituted in 1954, the Bharat Ratna is awarded for exceptional service of the highest order.

questions.question: The Dronacharya Award is given for excellence in sports ____.
questions.explanation: Instituted in 1985, it honours outstanding coaches in sports and games.

questions.question: Bihu is the famous folk dance and harvest festival of ____.
questions.explanation: Assam celebrates Rongali (Bohag), Kongali (Kati), and Bhogali (Magh) Bihu.

questions.question: The Thomas Cup is associated with the sport of ____.
questions.explanation: Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship in badminton (Uber Cup is for women).

questions.question: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated annually in the state of ____.
questions.explanation: Called the 'Festival of Festivals', it takes place every December in Kisama, Nagaland.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is headquartered at The Hague in the ____.
questions.explanation: The ICJ sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

sections.name: History & Monuments
sections.description: Ancient, medieval, modern Indian history, and UNESCO heritage sites

questions.question: The Great Bath was discovered at the Indus Valley site of ____.
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-daro (in present-day Sindh, Pakistan) featured the Great Bath and advanced drainage.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at ____.
questions.explanation: Known as Dharmachakrapravartana, the first sermon was delivered at Deer Park in Sarnath near Varanasi.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey was fought in the year ____.
questions.explanation: On 23 June 1757, Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, marking the rise of British rule.

questions.question: The founder of the Maurya Empire was ____.
questions.explanation: With Chanakya's guidance, Chandragupta Maurya established the Maurya Empire in ~322 BCE.

questions.question: The Sun Temple at Konark was built by King ____ I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
questions.explanation: Built in the 13th century in Odisha, Konark Sun Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in August ____.
questions.explanation: Launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the AICC with the call 'Do or Die'.

questions.question: The Ajanta and Ellora caves are located near Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) in ____.
questions.explanation: Both Ajanta and Ellora are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Maharashtra.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 in Bombay; its first President was ____.
questions.explanation: A. O. Hume helped organize the first session, which was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

questions.question: The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by ____.
questions.explanation: Completed in 1010 CE, it is a masterpiece of Chola architecture in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April ____.
questions.explanation: Occurred in Amritsar, Punjab on Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919.
